_comment: The eval profile: the exam pipeline at a price a table of four briefs can afford. Three chapters and a short word band, so every stage, every critic and the whole gate run exactly as they do for the exam novel - the only things made smaller are the number of chapters and their length. A profile is partial: it states what it changes and nothing else.
_comment_one_chapter: One chapter, not three: the owner's decision of 2026-09-24 ("super si eso me gusta", docs/spec.md §8). Every validator still runs on it; the example novel stays at ten.
_comment_why_not_tiny: Because `tiny` also shrinks the Story Bible to a cast of three, and an eval that scores continuity against a cast of three is not measuring what the exam novel does. The bible counts here are the exam's, unchanged - a brief that plants four mysteries has to have four mysteries to plant.
_comment_budget: 25.0, and the figure has a reason rather than a feeling behind it. The exam profile is 60.0 for ten chapters of 1,250 words; this is three chapters of 420, which is about a seventh of the prose - but the floor does not shrink with the book. Every unit still pays its ~48,800-token arrival (novaforge-v2 domain-knowledge 8.8), the Bible is the same size, and each chapter still faces six characteristics and up to three attempts. So a fifth of the exam's ceiling rather than a seventh, and four briefs at this figure is the outer bound the table was priced at.
_comment_models: Owner, 2026-09-24 (spec §8): the orchestrator on Sonnet - cheaper and faster than the session model; never Haiku, on which it stopped dispatching the project's agents.
